item: The mirror's name folding (lowercase after NFC) differs from APFS in rare cases such as ß and SS; it errs toward treating the file as the ow…
reason: The defect is still there: aliases() puts an NFC+lowercase gate in front of the inode/realpath test, so a rename between spellings that APFS treats as one name (ß/SS, final sigma, ligatures) is logged as foreign, not written, and its old spelling is swept. The artifact stays out of the mirror until its next change or the next host start. No owner file is touched. The realistic fix is to drop the gate and let the existing device/inode + realpath test decide; one change in aliases() covers both the write lookup and the stale sweep.
source: verified against code
evidence: src/engine-host/library/mirror.ts:644-646 — aliases() returns false whenever name.normalize('NFC').toLowerCase() differs, before its device/inode and realpath test runs

src/engine-host/library/mirror.ts:389-392 — the write's alias lookup (sameAs) goes through aliases(); on a fold miss the target counts as occupied and is logged as "not the mirror's file; not written"
src/engine-host/library/mirror.ts:419-426 — the stale sweep calls the same aliases() and then removeFile on the old spelling
src/artifacts/library/mirror.ts:69-84 — mirrorSlug keeps the title's case and characters (NFC only), so 'Straße' and 'STRASSE' give distinct strings that APFS stores as one entry

probe on this Mac's APFS (/tmp/maws-review/p4triage/exp-mirror-scripts/apfs.mjs, rename.mjs): Straße/STRASSE, Straße/strasse, οδος/οδοσ and ﬁle/file are one entry (same inode; realpath gives the stored spelling) while the fold says they differ; realpathSync.native keeps each hard link's own name (original.html vs backup.html, any lookup order, case variants included); a rename between two such spellings succeeds, and the old spelling then still aliases the new entry
git 48b17c7f9 added the fold to tell an owner's hard link apart; 485257d96 added realpath, which now does that job (mirror.ts:639-643 calls the fold 'a cheap first test')

src/engine-host/library/mirror.test.ts:241-259 — the hard-link case is rejected today by the fold; without the gate it is rejected by realpath (the probe shows that holds on APFS; on Linux realpath is path-only)
notes: Route choice: an APFS-matching fold is not realistic. JS has no case-fold primitive (toLowerCase is not folding; toUpperCase().toLowerCase() only approximates it). APFS's fold table follows Apple's Unicode version and its own normalization. Other volumes (case-sensitive APFS, HFS+, SMB, exFAT) fold differently again. And a fold adds no safety now that realpath separates hard links. So asking the filesystem (lstat dev/ino + realpath) is exact by construction. The row's wording 'extended to the stale sweep' is stale: since 48b17c7f9 the sweep already calls the same aliases(); what blocks both callers is the gate in front. Fixing only the write lookup would be harmful: after a rename the old spelling still aliases the new entry, so a sweep that still used the fold would delete the file it just renamed. Cost: without the gate, aliases() costs 2 lstats per pair, and both callers compare names pairwise (mine × new names), so a slug rename of an N-file artifact would make about 2N² synchronous lstats. The worker should lstat each name once and match by dev/ino, with realpath only on a match. Optional: require realDirsUnder for both names inside aliases(). Without the fold, two paths through a parent-folder link become aliases. The write path already refuses that case before its rename (:395), but the sweep would drop such a name instead of throwing (see L249). The row understates the effect slightly: the skip leaves the artifact unmirrored until its next change and logs a false 'not the mirror's file' line.
test: node project, mirror.test.ts: an unguarded case in the style of 'keeps the mirror of an artifact renamed by case only' (:192), with 'Straße' renamed to 'STRASSE' (and a final-sigma pair). Expect the listing [manifest, new name], the content, the entry's files and no logs. It is red before only on case-insensitive APFS and passes either way on Linux. The hard-link case :241 must stay green.
mac_why: The regression discriminates only on a case-insensitive APFS volume (the Mac's tmpdir), and mirror.test.ts is a §6-guarded file, so the gate rule runs unit:darwin on the mini (under a minute). The red-before run is a named-file vitest on a Mac through the slot.

reason: The defect is real, and the window is one lifeline fork and exec. The clause's fix (a single spawn whose shell forks the lifeline and then execs the server) is a transport redesign, not a bounded patch. It changes how the group drains on close, how a lost lifeline is detected, and the 'nothing passes through a shell' launch-fidelity claim, and its proof is a measured Mac scene.
source: verified against code
evidence: src/engine-host/connectors/direct-stdio.ts:40-44 — stdioSpawnPlan returns two separate spawns: the server (detached, so it leads its own group) and lifeline(group), which takes the server's pid and so can only be spawned after it

The two spawns run in one synchronous turn, but the lifeline's uv_spawn (a fork and exec) is the window. If the host is SIGKILLed there, the server's group is left with no lifeline, and stdin EOF is its only cover

src/engine-host/connectors/direct-stdio.ts:112 — ready waits for both 'spawn' events, and a lifeline that fails to start or exits early fails closed (watch, :137-149). That covers soft failures only, not a hard death

src/engine-host/connectors/direct-stdio.ts:230-238 — hasMembers polls the group until it is empty. A lifeline moved into the server's group (the single-spawn shape) would keep the group non-empty, so close and leader-exit semantics change too

docs/doperpowers/plans/2026-10-17-p3-hd-direct-route.md:240 (child DL17) and p3-co-work DL101 — closing requires a single spawn carrying the lifeline plus a hard-death test, with no native guardian. triage.txt:224 re-deferred it as a larger hardening change
notes: Checked on this Mac: `env -i FOO=bar /bin/sh -c 'exec /usr/bin/env'` prints FOO, PWD and SHLVL. So a shell-fork-then-exec construction hands the server PWD and SHLVL that the launch did not configure, unless the script strips them without clobbering configured ones. That breaks the transport header's claim of an exact materialized env with nothing through a shell (direct-stdio.ts:6-8). A lifeline that is not a separate ChildProcess needs another way to detect its loss without polling, e.g. an extra stdio fd whose end the host reads. The pid getter's 'server pid == group id' holds under exec but not under fork. Cheaper partial option that does not meet the closing clause: pre-spawn the lifeline, spawn the server, then write the server's pid to the lifeline's pipe in the same synchronous turn. That shrinks the window from a fork and exec to one write. A Node launcher is ruled out because the lifeline must not depend on the replaceable app binary (E10, direct-stdio.ts:12-15). Residual risk is tiny: a hard host death in a millisecond window, plus a server descendant that ignores EOF.
